messages:
mike: CI on main turned red right after the lockfile regen. Failing on mac-arm64 runners only. quick run showed a segfault in test_utils when importing our C extension.
laura: ugh. which package changed? any new native wheels?
mike: looks like pybind11 bumped transitive from 2.8.x -> 2.9.x and build tags have platform markers now. pip resolved a linux wheel on amd64 but for arm64 it picked a different wheel variant that appears to crash.
ria: can you paste the failing test log?
mike: sure — truncated: 
```
=========================== short test summary ============================
FAILED test_utils.py::test_kv_cache_init - Segmentation fault (core dumped)
--- last lines ---
ImportError: dynamic module does not define module export function (PyInit__cext)
```
laura: that ImportError usually means ABI mismatch or a different compiler flag. Did the wheel for that transitive dep change its tag?
mike: grabbed the wheel names from the runner cache:
```
pybind11-2.9.0-cp38-cp38-macosx_11_0_arm64.whl
pybind11-2.8.1-cp38-cp38-macosx_11_0_arm64.whl
```
ops-bot: @channel CI failure detected on main (mac-arm64). Linked builds: https://ci/internal/4056789
sebastian: can we repro locally on an M1 machine? I can try, but need a quick bisect to narrow which transitive pin introduced the bad wheel.
ria: try `pip debug --verbose` inside the venv from the failing job to see why resolver picked that wheel. also check lockfile for markers in poetry's lock (markers like "platform_system").
mike: ran pip debug, resolver notes show: 
```
Found link for pybind11 from simple index: platform_macos_arm64 -> prefer wheel with macosx_11_0_arm64
```
and part of pyproject.lock shows an extra "platform": "macos_11_arm64" entry (wasn't in previous lock).
laura: hypothesis: our lock regen picked a new build artifact from upstream that set manylinux tags for arm, and poetry included it for arm64. Could be the upstream wheel was accidentally built against a different Python API.
ria: could you run our dep-bisect script to pin pybind11 back to 2.8.1 in a job matrix and see if tests pass? If so, we know it's the wheel change.
mike: kicking off a quick bisect job now (matrix: pybind11==2.8.1 and 2.9.0). I'll paste results.
ci-bot: Job queued: dep-bisect/4056790001 (matrix: pybind11@2.8.1,2.9.0)
mike: 4056790280 — pybind11==2.8.1 job passed on mac-arm64. 4056790356 — 2.9.0 failed with same segfault.
sebastian: good, that nails it to pybind11 wheel variant. Next steps: either pin pybind11 in our lockfile back to 2.8.x pending upstream fix, or contact upstream to publish a corrected arm64 wheel.
laura: for a fast fix I vote pin + hotfix release. can someone open a tiny PR to add a constraints entry (pybind11==2.8.1) and trigger CI?
mike: opening PR now, will include changelog note and an issue for upstream contact.
ria: also add a CI check to fail lock regen if it introduces new platform-specific markers without approval — we keep hitting these ABI surprises.
sebastian: agree. created an issue: https://issues/internal/REDWOOD-2345 to track non-automatic platform marker additions and add an automation.
mike: PR up: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/4023 — requesting review from @laura and @sebastian.
laura: reviewing now, will merge once green. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: auto-retry scheduled: rerun with constraints patch after merge.
